admission.justification: A failed or refused read leaves the same tall tree in place: without the status reveal the reader saw no statement that the read had failed and needed the Jump control, which OR-R042's ruling closed as an answered-only gap. The reveal is realized in the workspace's selection-focus effect, its ten mounted cases and the captured HTTP 400 refusal.

applicability: The mounted intent reviewer's reading area after an in-tree selection on the stacked layout whose read ends failed or refused.
conditions: The status reading area is scrolled into view; the selection mark stays on the requested row and the tree keeps every row.
The reveal moves no focus and leaves the selection's focus request in place, so a successful retry still lands focus as an answer does.
The reveal happens only when the selection was in-tree, the layout is stacked, and the reader has not moved focus while the read was on its way.
exclusions: Wide layouts and outside selections: their surface position is unchanged.
The pending phase: the view stays where it is until the read settles.
Request counts and the reading area's content, which the read cycle and the failure block own.

evidence: browser/final/facts-unavailable.json, facts-retry.json and browser/new-vs-reviewed.json; mutations R-a, R-b, R-c, R-f in mutations/summary.json of this pass's evidence folder

statement: On the stacked layout an in-tree selection whose read fails or is refused scrolls the reading area that states that status into view, unless the reader moved focus while the read was on its way; it moves no focus and leaves the selection's focus request for a retry.
